title: SemantiK Pedagogical Lexicon
description: Profile-organized vocabulary of pedagogical opener labels, end-of-chapter apparatus section names, and OCR-confusable normalizations consumed by the SemantiK adapter seam (lib/semantik/opener_classifier.py, lib/semantik/heading_classifier.py, and the marker-normalization pass in lib/semantik/adapter.py). Wave #22 (tiers 1-2 semantic enrichment) lifted these vocabularies out of hardcoded Python constants so a NEW corpus is onboarded by adding a PROFILE / label entry here, never by editing code (the owner's directive 3: lexicon profiles, not corpus-specific code). Profile selection is env-driven via SEMANTIK_LEXICON_PROFILE (default 'generic-academic+openstax'): a '+'-joined list of profile keys merged left-to-right, the later profile OVERLAYING the earlier one. Beyond the two default profiles, two composite-unit overlays generalize the tier-2 planner past learning-science textbooks: 'scholarly' (theorem/lemma/proof apparatus -> theorem_block composite units) and 'admonition' (note/warning/tip callouts common in technical docs / mkdocs -> admonition composite units); both are opt-in overlays (e.g. 'generic-academic+scholarly') and change NOTHING for the default profiles.
$comment: Vocabularies lifted verbatim (behavior-preserving refactor) from: opener_classifier._OPENERS + _INTERIOR_OPENERS (the six promotable openers and the three interior-split-capable numbered ones); heading_classifier.APPARATUS_HEADING_NAMES (standalone + leading-split apparatus section headings), _INTERIOR_APPARATUS_NAMES (the ALL-CAPS interior-banner subset), and _APPARATUS_WHITELIST (short-heading demotion whitelist); and adapter._CONFUSABLE_TRYIT_RE (the trvit->TRY IT OCR-confusable). The abstract 'association_role' on each opener is the Wave #22 Tier-2 composite-unit vocabulary (worked_example example/solution/practice, procedure, section_opener objectives/readiness) the adapter's _associate_composite_units pass keys on; it maps each concrete opener role slug to the abstract role the association rules are expressed over. Build #23 Tier-3 adds a 'subclasses' section per profile: a dict keyed by composite-unit TYPE (worked_example / exercise_set / definition_group / procedure / section_opener / figure_group) plus the rhetorical 'prose' key, each mapping to the SEED vocabulary of kebab-case subclass labels the model-assisted subclassifier (lib/semantik/subclassifier.py, gated by SEMANTIK_SEMANTIC_SUBCLASS) picks from OR extends. Merged across profiles by per-unit-type list concatenation (get_lexicon_subclasses); a genuinely-new model-proposed label is accepted onto the emitted HTML but LOGGED to a review sidecar, never silently canonized into this file. label 'pattern' values are regex BODY fragments (word-internal whitespace is \s+): the classifiers wrap them with the shared gutter / number / anchor scaffolding (opener_classifier._GUTTER / _NUM), so a pattern is corpus VOCAB only, never structural regex.

generic-academic.description: Default academic-textbook vocabulary (Example / Solution / How To openers, the Key-Terms-class end-of-chapter apparatus sections, and the short-heading whitelist). Corpus-agnostic: the labels a mathematics / science / humanities textbook uses regardless of publisher.

worked_example.application-problem: the task is posed in a real-world or narrative context (quantities with units, money, objects, people, scenarios), even when the worked solution itself is purely symbolic
worked_example.symbolic-manipulation: pure expression rewriting, simplification, or equation solving with no surrounding real-world context
worked_example.conceptual-illustration: demonstrates WHY an idea or property holds (a pattern, picture, or counterexample) rather than solving a posed task
worked_example.multi-step-procedure: walks through a named multi-stage procedure where the sequence of steps is itself the point

exercise_set.drill: repetitive practice of one isolated skill
exercise_set.word-problems: practice problems posed in narrative or real-world contexts
exercise_set.mixed-review: mixed practice spanning several earlier topics

definition_group.term-glossary: introduces vocabulary terms and their meanings

procedure.algorithm: a fixed step-by-step method that always runs the same way
procedure.strategy: a heuristic or decision guide requiring judgment about when and how to apply it

section_opener.objectives-overview: lists what the reader will learn in the section
section_opener.readiness-check: a prerequisite self-check to complete before starting the section

figure_group.diagram-series: a sequence of related diagrams or illustrations

prose.claim-evidence: asserts a claim and supports it with evidence or reasoning
prose.problem-solution: describes a problem and then presents its resolution

openstax.description: OpenStax-specific overlay: the TRY IT (practice) / BE PREPARED (readiness) numbered openers, and the trvit->TRY IT OCR-confusable the sample-algebra scan corpus emits. Overlays the generic-academic profile without displacing it.

scholarly.description: Scholarly-apparatus overlay for mathematics / theoretical texts: the theorem-environment openers (Theorem / Lemma / Proposition / Corollary / Proof / Definition / Remark / Notation). Designed to overlay generic-academic (e.g. SEMANTIK_LEXICON_PROFILE=generic-academic+scholarly) so Example / Solution keep flowing through the generic worked_example machinery. A theorem STATEMENT (association_role 'theorem') plus its following proof (association_role 'proof') and any trailing remarks / corollaries (association_role 'remark') coagulate into one theorem_block composite unit; Definition (+ Example) groups via the existing definition_group shape. Corpus-agnostic: these are the labels any scholarly discipline uses, not a publisher's house style.

theorem_block.theorem-proof: a theorem statement followed by its proof
theorem_block.lemma-proof: an auxiliary lemma with proof supporting a larger result
theorem_block.corollary-remark: a corollary or remark following from a nearby result

definition_group.formal-definition: a rigorous formal definition of a concept

admonition.description: Admonition-callout overlay for technical documentation / mkdocs-style corpora: the note / warning / tip / caution / important / danger / attention / hint labels. Each admonition label plus its body coagulates into one admonition composite unit (a SINGLETON unit type — a single labelled callout is a complete unit) whose accessible name is the label. Overlay on generic-academic (e.g. SEMANTIK_LEXICON_PROFILE=generic-academic+admonition). Corpus-agnostic: the canonical admonition vocabulary shared across reStructuredText / Material-for-mkdocs / DocBook, not one project's callouts.

admonition.warning: risk of harm, data loss, or serious error
admonition.tip: a helpful shortcut or best practice
admonition.caution: requires care; easy to get wrong
